_what: Every setting of the run; FEATURES.md says what each means.

years._what: puf is the PUF's tax year; target is the tax year of the file being built.

paths._what: out is the folder every stage writes under (REBUILD_OUT overrides it); raw holds the input files, which are only read.

raw._scf_wave_dirs: The folder of an SCF wave whose files are not yet in the shared raw-data folder, used in place of the scf path.
raw._soi_tables: The local copy of SOI's tables: the shared mirror plus Tables 1.3 and 4.3 as tidy files.
raw._soi_w2: SOI's Form W-2 statistics (Table 4.B, by filing status), read for the tips targets.
raw._pce: NIPA personal consumption expenditures by the CEX's eight categories, in billions of dollars; a bare file name is read from research/rebuild/resources/growth.
raw._cps_earnings: The CPS ASEC extract with the earnings questions, occupation, industry and class of worker, read by overtime_cps.R.
raw._cps_march_basic: The CPS March basic monthly and ASEC samples linked by MARBASECIDP, for hours last week at the main job and for the earnings of the month-4 group missing from the March 2024 ASEC; null leaves both out.
raw._eap_codes: The Department of Labor's 2016 white-collar duties classes by occupation, from Tedeschi's overtime report (The Budget Lab, September 2024).
raw._cps_repwt: The CPS ASEC's 160 person replicate weights, for the standard errors of the CPS overtime targets.
raw._z1: The Federal Reserve's Financial Accounts (Z.1) CSV files, read for the yearly revaluation rates (table S1M.i.a).
raw._census_pep: Census population estimates by state, sex, race, Hispanic origin and single year of age, summed to national counts for the death probabilities' check.

inheritance._what: Inheritances received in the income year, an SCF-only slot. The SCF rounds the year received to the nearest 5, so each reported inheritance counts as received in the income year with the chance year_weights gives its year code ({wave: {year code: chance}}, 0 for codes not listed), following Gale and Sabelhaus (2024); gifts of gift_type are left out, and salt seeds the keyed draws.

network._what: The network's size: the width of each slot's vector, layers, attention heads, the width inside each layer's feed-forward block (ffn), and dropout.

training._what: Training: seed and passes (REBUILD_SEED and REBUILD_PASSES override them), records per step (batch), the learning rate's schedule, weight decay, and the share of the table held back to measure the fit.

translation._what: The translation table: one row per survey variable shared with the PUF, with how the survey's amount is defined (items, first_year, part, loss_cap, less_traditional_deferrals), how function 1 maps it beyond the dollar line (dollar_line, loss_line, match, rank_against; a null line keeps dollars throughout, a line of 0 maps by rank throughout), and whether function 2 fills in (fill_in). Each row's reason says why it departs from the default of dollars and no fill-in. report_lines are the dollar lines of the report's size ranges. See FEATURES.md, "Translation: putting the surveys on the PUF's terms".

translation._cps_zero_in_tax_data: PUF amounts the CPS does not have that the CPS units in the tax data carry as zero; the CPS's interest does not line up with the PUF's taxable interest.

cex._what: The CEX interview survey, one row per tax unit and quarterly interview, a shared household's spending divided among its tax units by head count. Its eight consumption categories are drawn last at generation, at the record's own CEX year.
cex._generation_year: The year of the single-year dollar maps, used only for frames without a survey year column.

cps._what: The CPS ASEC by tax year: every tax unit as the filing stage built them, filers and non-filers. Training draws the filing flag from p_file in every pass; filer is one fixed draw (filer_seed plus the year) for checks and reports; dollar_amounts are grown to the target year by SOI's wages per return.
cps._generation_year: The year of the single-year dollar maps, used only for frames without a survey year column.
cps._step1_dir: The filing stage's folder inside the data folder: the CPS's tax units, the filing requirement, the returns and the checks.
cps._step1_out: The folder inside step1_dir that holds the filing stage's returns, read by build_cps.R.

overtime._what: Each person's overtime pay by the FLSA rules (overtime_cps.R): salary_threshold is the weekly salary level by tax year, hce_annual the highly compensated employee line, computer_hourly the computer-employee hourly line, and seed the duties-test draw (plus the year).

sipp._what: The SIPP by reference year, its households split into tax units by the shared rules. Its tips slots (each adult's tips, and whether they are mostly from leisure and hospitality) are drawn last at generation; the file holds each person's tips to at most that person's wages.
sipp._years: Reference years, the same as the CPS's: 2015 is the 2014 panel's wave 3, and later years are the annual releases.
sipp._generation_year: The year of the single-year dollar maps, used only for frames without a survey year column.
sipp._lh_industries: Leisure and hospitality: Census industry codes 8560-8690 (NAICS 71 and 72). The range starts at 8560 to cover the 2014 panel's older codes.
sipp._lh_share: A person's tips count as leisure and hospitality when more than this share of them comes from such jobs.
sipp._mfs_salt: The salt of the keyed draw that splits joint couples into separate returns until they reach SOI Table 1.6's separate returns.

deferrals._what: Elective deferrals to 401(k)-type plans. Each person's are held to the legal limit for their age (limits: [under 50, 50 and over]) and to their wages. The traditional part, elective x (1 - roth_share), is subtracted from a survey's gross wages to give the link wage, and in the file it is Tax-Simulator's trad_contr_er1 and trad_contr_er2.
deferrals._limits: The section 402(g) limit and catch-up by tax year, as published through 2026 (SECURE 2.0's age 60-63 catch-up left out); later years grow 2.4% a year, rounded down to $500 as the law indexes them.
deferrals._roth_share: The Roth share of elective contributions, joint and non-joint returns, from SOI's W-2 statistics; years after 2020 take 2020's.
deferrals._sipp_item: The SIPP's own 401(k), 403(b), 503(b) and Thrift Savings Plan contributions, asked only for reference years 2021 and 2023; in earlier years they are missing and the link wage is gross wages.

filing._what: The CPS filing stage: each tax unit's chance of filing, logit(chance) = a(age band of the head) + k x (child under 17) + required x (r + s x log gross income + b x (business or farm income)), with log income centred on the weighted median among required units. The 11 parameters are solved each year to hit non-filing adults in 7 age bands and the shares below. Dependents file their own return if required to or if they have wages.
filing._child_share: Non-filing children under 17 as a share of CPS children under 17, held at the 2015 share: Census PEP children less the 2015 PUF's child credit children, over Census PEP children.
filing._required_nonfiling_share: Non-filing units among units required to file: Pub 5785 Table 3's 11.19 million (tax years 2014-16) over 118.53 million required units in the 2015 CPS.
filing._income_share: Required non-filers' gross income as a share of all required units' gross income: Pub 5785 Table 3's $409.4 billion over $8,987.5 billion in the 2015 CPS.
filing._business_share: Required non-filers with business or farm income as a share of required non-filers: 4.99 of 11.19 million (Pub 5785 Table 3).
filing._mfs_salt: The salt of the keyed order in which joint couples are split into separate returns, until weight times calibrated chance reaches half of SOI Table 1.6's separate returns.
filing._age_shape: Adults on returns by age band (SOI Pub 1304 Table 1.6) and Census PEP adults (checks only), per year.
filing._pep_children: Census PEP national population under 17 and under 18 by tax year, used in the checks only.

ages._what: The primary filer's age range. PUF records with no range get probabilities calibrated to SOI Table 1.6 in cells where at least min_missing_share of the weight has none; in survey couples the primary is chosen to match the PUF's share of female primaries by range.

earn_split._what: The split of a married couple's earnings. spouse_se_share is E30500 / E30400 on the PUF, and earn_split is the demographic file's EARNSPLIT code (1 primary 75% or more, 2 25-75%, 3 under 25%, 0 none), predicted by a gradient boosted classifier (model) where demographics are missing. se_factor and se_floor are Schedule SE's 92.35% and $400; check_agi and booklet_full_less_public are for checks only.
earn_split._part_se: How part_se is read from the PUF's self-employment tax: the two Schedule SE rates, the 2015 Social Security wage base ($118,500), and the share and dollar gap beyond which earnings differ from 92.35% of Schedules C and F by more than rounding.

blindness._what: The PUF reading behind the blindness rule: on unmarried returns taking the standard deduction, the deduction above the 2015 basic amount, in units of the additional amount, is the number of extra boxes; whole_tolerance is how far from a whole number that may be.

generation._what: The filer batch and the non-filer batch; every filer record's AGI group label is preset and everything else is drawn given it.
generation._filers: synthetic draws the filer records from the networks. real_puf uses every 2015 PUF record with its own PUF items and the networks drawing the rest, keeps the PUF's aggregate records (so hidden_returns is off), and runs the package stage after taxsim_file.
generation._label: label_records filer records over all models, split across the 12 band-AGI groups in proportion to the PUF's records, each weighted by its group's 2015 PUF returns over the records drawn in it; label_seed seeds the draws.
generation._scf_wave_seed: The seed of each record's SCF wave draw, made with the shares in the year's prior.yaml.
generation._survey_year_seeds: The seeds of each record's CEX, CPS and SIPP year draws, made with the shares in the year's prior.yaml.
generation._nonfiler_records: The non-filer batch, drawn under the CPS label with the filing flag 0 and every weight 1; its size is label_records times the CPS's expected non-filers over SOI's returns, and nonfiler_seed seeds it.
generation._models: The trained models pooled into each year's file, each drawing an equal share with its own seeds (seed_shift added) and record ids from k x 10,000,000; null uses the run's own model alone.

top_hidden._what: The rebuild of the 2015 PUF's four aggregate records as synthetic returns made from generated records (top_hidden.py).
top_hidden._candidate_records: Candidate filer records for the rebuild by the 12 band-AGI groups, each weighted by its group's 2015 PUF returns over the records drawn in it; groups at 0 are not drawn.
top_hidden._candidate_seed: The candidates' generation seed, separate from label_seed so no draw of the file moves.
top_hidden._selection: SOI's rule for the aggregate records (Bryant, Czajka, Ivsin and Nunns 2014), in population weight: the top 400 returns by AGI, the 30 highest of each income item and lowest of each loss, and the 10 highest or lowest of most other fields.
top_hidden._records_per_group: At most this many chosen records per aggregate group, sampled in proportion to weight, plus up to min_per_rule records for each selection rule the sample lacks.
top_hidden._targeted_per_gap: Where a group needs a sign of a field that its chosen records lack, this many candidates that have it are added, largest first.
top_hidden._count_tolerance: The standard error of each booklet count in the reweighting at tau 1: the larger of this many returns and this share of the count.
top_hidden._group_iterations: After scaling, a record whose AGI has left its group is moved (the first move_iterations rounds) or dropped (later rounds), and the weights and scaling are done again.
top_hidden._wealth: Each rebuilt return's balance sheet is drawn again under the SCF label, up to wealth_tries times, until net worth is below wealth_cap; a record that never gets below keeps its lowest try and is flagged.
top_hidden._id_block: The first record id of the rebuilt returns.

consistency._what: When an item in when_any_nonzero is nonzero, at least one holding in then_at_least_one_nonzero must be; offset_generations is how many times generation runs to offset the rule's effect on holders (1 means no offset).

rules.name: a partnership or S corporation item

dollars._what: seed: the seed of the draws that pick each record's dollars within its band.
dollars._scf_caps: Balance-sheet items whose dollar map is held to a percentile among the wave's holders, so that the SCF's largest amounts do not land on ordinary records.

tilt._what: Reweighting: the start's weights are scaled, then moved to minimize the misses on the year's targets plus the size of the move. The targets are in targets_config/.
tilt._precheck: A check before the reweighting that only reports: a target is flagged when the average it requires lies outside the records' range by more than min_excess_se standard errors, its relative standard error is below min_relative_se, or the start is more than max_start_gap_se standard errors from it.
tilt._reweighting: The cost: the sum over targets of 0.5 x importance x (miss / standard error)^2 plus tau x the Kullback-Leibler move from the start, with identities exact. newton_budget is the most Newton steps in all, gradient_tolerance the stopping size, average_weight_change the move in a group's weight that triggers a second solve for the standard errors of averages, and importance_one_kinds the target kinds with importance 1 (the others 1 / other_importance_divisor).

interest_growth._what: From from_year on, taxable interest grows with rate_series (nominal GDP times CBO's 3-month Treasury bill rate), and non-qualified dividends with a blend of their own series and rate_series weighted by the start file's split; enabled false turns this off.

tilt._projection: The projection years' steps (projection_steps.py): population_dir is CBO's population by marital status and age; items_table each grown column's series and target; add_factors_table extra growth by item and years, each non-zero row with a note; return_age_edges the age bands of the returns targets; cbo_last_year the last year of CBO projections, with long-run Macro-Projections growth after it; item_min_records and item_min_dollars the floors for an item's target; filing_season the blend of SOI's November filing-season tables with CBO's growth for the first projection year. See FEATURES.md, "Projection years".
tilt._soft_cap: A soft cap on each record's weight: U is k times the mean starting weight of the record's AGI group, and the cost adds 0.5 x beta x ((w - U) / U)^2 above U; k null means no cap.
tilt._top: The top of the file: enabled adds the Forbes records and limits the SCF targets to units below $1 billion; billionaire_lists are the Forbes lists by year (weight 1, held fixed) and after_last_list says how later years grow the last list; hidden_returns turns on the rebuild of the PUF's aggregate records; redraw_tries and its seeds redraw a generated balance sheet of $1 billion or more; stand_in_agi and stand_in_min_records set the billionaires' item mix without the rebuilt top group; gift_rate_top and gift_rate_rest are gifts as a share of wealth (BSYZ 2025, Table 2). See FEATURES.md, "The top of the file".

non_micro_imputations._what: Items set from what the model has drawn plus a published table, with no new microdata, run inside the reweighting stage on the start before the solve. Each item lists the columns it reads and writes, its tables in resources/non_micro/ and its random stream; an item changes a drawn column only if it lists it in writes_back.
non_micro_imputations._salt_base: Every random number is ages.uniform_by_id(record_id, salt_base + 8 x stream + person), person 0 for the unit, 1 and 2 for the adults and 3 to 5 for dependents, so a draw never moves when other records change. Streams are never renumbered; stream 3 is unused.

dependent_filer_age_sex._why: Each dependent filer gets an exact age and sex drawn from the CPS dependents who file their own return, in the record's CPS year and age range, keyed by record id; ages above top_age are set to top_age.

child_credit._why: Dependent k passes every child credit test except age and Social Security number when under 17 and n_dep_ctc is at least k; dependents from 17 to the law's age limit less one pass by chance, as in production. 1 passes, 0 not, -1 no such dependent.

death_probabilities._why: The SSA period life table by year, age and sex, times Chetty et al.'s mortality ratio at the person's income percentile, times for men Johnson et al.'s marital factor, as in production; no draw. Stream 8 gives a sex to a primary filer with an age but no sex.

unrealized_gains._why: Each asset's value times the year's Z.1 revaluation rate for its kind; retirement accounts use the drawn stock share, and years without a full year of Z.1 data use production's long-run rates.

cost_basis._why: Basis is value less the SCF's unrealized gain, each gain first held to the value; other real estate's gain is split between other homes and other real estate by value, as in production.

gains_holding_period._why: A holding-period group drawn with SOCA's shares of long-term gain dollars, an exact period from a Weibull shape, and basis from production's regression on SOCA's panel; each period is held between 1 year and the older adult's age less 18.

reads: the income items of production's measure
parents_rank._why: Each unit's income percentile (the bottom 10 merged into rank 10), then a parent rank drawn from Chetty et al.'s matrix, as production intends.

blindness._why: Each primary filer, and each spouse on a joint return, is blind with the 2015 PUF's rate for their age range times one factor per person type, set so that the filers' count matches Publication 4801's blind boxes for the year.

reads: the partnership and S corporation parts
qbi._why: QBI wages: a filing record's wages in a business group are its drawn number of outside workers times a yearly scalar that makes the file's total equal the IRS total (grown with wages per return after the table's last year). Schedule C and F wages go to wagebill_sole_prop; partnership and S corporation wages are split by positive income. The specified-service flag is one draw per SCF industry group, c_by_scf_group being the share of self-employed people there in the law's listed industries; farms are never specified service and their wage bill is positive farm income.

amt_nol_cap._why: The AMT net operating loss adjustment is held to the record's net operating loss, the negative part of other_agi_remainder (Form 1040 line 21), since the model draws the two separately; the drawn value is kept as amt_nols_drawn.

taxes._what: Taxes under the target year's law, computed inside the reweighting stage before the solve by tax-simulator-gpu's batch command, from a copy of its repository at commit, run with its own Python (python); the columns join the file as calc_<name>.
taxes._draw_seed: The seed of the calculator's draws keyed by record id, such as child care credit take-up and the state tax workaround's owners.
taxes._wage_increment: Dollars added to the primary earner's wages for the marginal tax rates on wages; 0 skips them.

repealed_adjustments._what: Each adjustment and the first tax year the law no longer allows it; taxes.py sets it to zero and moves the adjustments total and other_agi with it.

taxes._refund_tax_benefit_from: The first tax year the tax benefit rule applies to state refunds: a refund received in year t repays year t-1's taxes, and the cap on the taxes deduction began in 2018.
taxes._refund_reported_anyway: The chance that an itemizer whose refund the tax benefit rule removes reports it anyway, as SOI shows on about 5% of returns at AGI $2-5 million; 0 applies the rule alone.

greedy_schedule_a._what: In a year with SOI Table 2.1, each Schedule A category's input factor is set so that the start's dollars per claiming return match Table 2.1's; passes is the number of calculator runs, and max_move bounds the factor's distance from 1.

state_weights._what: State weights for every year: soi_cv and lib are the folders each past year links to (SOI's coefficients of variation, the pinned calculator); tolerance and nonfiler_tolerance set the state targets' standard errors; tau is as in tilt.reweighting, and newton_budget is the integrated solve's Newton steps a year. See FEATURES.md, "State weights".
